title: Learned birth-expression signature associates with later neonatal sepsis
summary: Retrospective LASSO analysis of blood collected while newborns appeared healthy identified a four-gene signature associated with early-onset sepsis during the following week. A small external diagnostic check gave AUC .72, but those external samples were collected after illness onset. This does not independently validate pre-symptom screening or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO; sparse partial least-squares discriminant analysis
organization: Simon Fraser University; University of British Columbia; London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

source_review.scope: Exact primary identity and scoped safe computational/clinical Methods and high-level Results; evidence access distinguished in case ledger; no operational laboratory procedures evaluated

evidence.tested: The prospective source cohort enrolled 720 newborns; day-of-birth expression comparisons included 14 later early-onset cases, six late-onset cases, 12 localized-infection cases and 32 healthy controls. Repeated development splits selected features; the final four-gene model used all available birth samples. The separate GSE26440 check comprised six early-onset cases and six controls.
evidence.unknown: Prospective sample collection does not establish that the fitted model was frozen before outcomes. The headline development AUC .94 is not a held-out future-patient estimate; Monte Carlo testing and final whole-cohort fitting are distinct analyses. External post-onset samples do not test prediction before clinical symptoms. Tiny case counts, clinical sepsis definitions and selected controls limit generalization. No prevention or causal immune-development mechanism is represented.
evidence.ai_role: Penalized model fitting selects and combines expression features linked to subsequent clinical status; the learned signature, not conventional differential expression alone, supplies the scoped finding.
